name: Lamprey
description: The lamprey is a primitive, eel-like fish without jaws. It belongs to the oldest still living vertebrates and has hardly changed since 360 million years.
habitat: Lampreys live in rivers and streams with sandy or muddy bottoms. Some species migrate to the sea and return to freshwater to spawn.
diet: Depending on species: larvae filter small organisms from sediment, adult parasitic species attach to fish
size: 15-30 cm (brook lamprey), up to 120 cm (sea lamprey)
weight: 50-150 g (small species), up to 2.5 kg (sea lamprey)
features: Seven gill openings on each side
Eyes appear like nine (hence the name)
conservation: In Germany critically endangered to threatened with extinction - strictly protected by EU directives
funFact: Lampreys are living fossils! They existed before dinosaurs and have survived the last five mass extinctions. Their body structure is so successful that it has hardly changed.
